q-103289:
Let's plot the graph of $y=tan⁡x.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13933873/assets/732955302ca49a41f6c43cf242d7c869e630e88d804c4b56a5beb3b081f2d230.png)

Let's go through each statement.

- Statement I is true. The function is defined everywhere, except where $x=\frac{\pi }{2}+n\pi .$

- Statement II is false. The zeros occur at $x=0,\pm \pi ,\pm 2\pi ,…,$ which can be written as $x=n\pi .$

- Statement III is false. The function takes values on all the real numbers, hence the range is $y\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$

So, the correct answer is "I only".

q-29608:
Let's recall the graph of $y=tan⁡x.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13933873/assets/31b430f003171dcc04a8f17402d6035fbbc305c244d3676bbf5da83fa447bd50.png)

Let's examine each statement.

- Statement I is false. The function $y=tan⁡x$ has asymptotes at $x=\frac{\pi }{2}+\pi n.$

- Statement II is true. The function has period $\pi .$ So, $tan⁡(x+2n\pi )=tan⁡(x+n\pi +n\pi )=tan⁡(x+n\pi )=tan⁡(x).$

- Statement III is false. The range of $y=tan⁡x$ is $(-\infty ,+\infty ).$
